## A first look at the DOM {#sec-dummy-dom}

The browser turns this HTML:

```html
<ul id="todos">
  <li>Buy milk</li>
  <li>Write code</li>
</ul>
```

into a tree of objects, and TypeScript can ask for them:

```ts
const list = document.querySelector<HTMLUListElement>("#todos");
const items = document.querySelectorAll("li");
console.log(items.length); // 2
```

::: {.callout-tip}
Every element in the tree is an **object**. That word follows you through the
whole book.
:::

::: {.research title="What does `querySelectorAll` give back?"}
The next exercise selects every `li` on the page and changes them all. The
book shows you the call and nothing more. Find out:

1. `document.querySelectorAll("li")` does not return an array. What does it
   return?
2. Name two different ways to visit every element of the result.
3. Your program adds a new `li` afterwards. Does the result contain it? What
   word does MDN use for this behaviour?

For the exam you need to be able to loop over the result without looking it
up.
:::
